title: Crosswalk region absent from the scene graph
statement: No node, edge or attribute marks a crosswalk. The entity type enumeration has no crosswalk constructor, and process_to_junction_rsv keeps only Driving nodes and collapses every other surface into the single Off Road node, so the region a clause conditions on cannot be located even approximately. I wanted a crosswalk entity a vehicle or a pedestrian could be `isIn`, or a landmark carrying the crossing code. CARLA's map exposes crosswalk polygons at capture time (carla.Map.get_crosswalks), so the datum exists in the simulator and not in the graph: a collector of our own, run at capture time, would let a rule say 'the ego entered a crosswalk' and 'a pedestrian is in the crosswalk ahead'. Until then the two pedestrian clauses cannot be formalized at all, and must not be approximated with a junction or an Off Road test, which name different regions.
evidence: carla/schema.json entity_types (no crosswalk constructor) and reading_guide.off_road_node, which records that sidewalk nodes are filtered out by process_to_junction_rsv and that every non-driving surface collapses into one Off Road node.

title: Stop line position absent from the scene graph
statement: Nothing in the graph marks where a vehicle is required to halt. A traffic light's `controls` edges are built from get_affected_lane_waypoints, the lanes the signal acts on; CARLA exposes the halt position separately as get_stop_waypoints and the generator never calls it. Lane, road and junction nodes carry no attributes at all, so no distance to a line can be computed on the other side either. I wanted a stop position, or an edge from a signal or sign to the place the approach must halt, which would let a rule say 'the ego crossed the line without having stopped short of it'. The nearest available quantity is the separation from the signal head, which is a different thing and would be an approximation, so it is not used. EX-STOP-002 is about the line itself and is blocked outright; EX-STOP-001 is formalized with the corresponding residue recorded on its node.
evidence: carla/schema.json governance_edges.what_is_still_absent and governance_edges.traffic_light_targets, which record that get_stop_waypoints exists and is never called, and reading_guide.node_coordinates, which records that structure nodes carry no attributes.

title: Non-ego vehicle motion state
statement: No non-ego actor carries a speed, a velocity or an acceleration: the generator writes the state and control channels for the ego node alone, and the only dynamic evidence about another vehicle is its light booleans. Its position is lifted per frame, but a scene predicate sees one frame, so 'that vehicle is stopped' is not derivable from the lifted keys. I wanted a non-ego velocity or speed so a rule could say 'another vehicle is stopped'. CARLA exposes get_velocity on every actor, so the datum exists in the simulator and not in the graph. Without it, a clause whose antecedent is another vehicle being stopped cannot be formalized, and reading its brake light instead would substitute an actuation for a motion state.
evidence: carla/schema.json attribute_keys, where `speed`, `accel` and the vel_*/acc_* channels are marked EGO ONLY, and reading_guide.vehicle_light_booleans, which records that the light booleans are the only dynamic evidence kept about a non-ego vehicle.

title: Road curvature discarded by the abstraction
statement: Nothing in the trace says whether the road bends. The generator computes a turn angle per waypoint on its base graph, and process_to_junction_rsv folds every waypoint of a lane into one attribute-free node, so none of it reaches the RSV; lane nodes carry no geometry from which it could be recovered. I wanted a curvature or turn-angle attribute on the lane a vehicle occupies, so that a rule could say 'the ego is on a curve'. The ego's own steering and yaw rate are not a substitute: a manoeuvre generates both on a perfectly straight road, which is exactly the case the clause distinguishes. Recording this `unsupported` would be wrong - the datum is computed and then thrown away, not missing.
evidence: perception/portability.json road_curvature, origin in_base_not_rsv, citing carla_sgg/sgg.py:314-339 for the computation and the abstraction for discarding it.

title: Road context: built-up area versus open road
statement: No attribute distinguishes a road inside a city or town from one outside it, or a freeway from an ordinary road: structure nodes carry no attributes at all, and no lifted key on an actor says anything about the road class. I wanted a road-context attribute on the lane or road a vehicle occupies. OpenDRIVE carries a road type element and CARLA exposes the map's OpenDRIVE at capture time, so the datum exists in the simulator and not in the graph. Without it the two default speed limits cannot be told apart and each is formalized with a residue in the opposite direction, and the 'high-speed road' and 'freeway' preconditions of two further clauses have no reading that is not an invented threshold on the ego's own speed.
evidence: carla/schema.json attribute_keys, which lists only road_id, lane_id and junction_id for structure, and reading_guide.node_coordinates, which records that lane, road and junction nodes are built attribute-free.

title: Weather and road surface state
statement: The trace says nothing about precipitation, standing water, wetness or fog, so a clause whose threshold is conditioned on 'good weather and road conditions' is formalized as if conditions were always good. I wanted the capture's weather block as a declared constant the adapter could put on the trace. CARLA's weather parameters are already written into each capture's simulation.json by the capture script, so this is a manifest the adapter does not read rather than a re-record. It would let a rule state the fair-weather threshold and the adverse-weather threshold separately instead of silently applying the lighter one.
evidence: perception/portability.json surface_and_weather_state, origin in_api_not_graph, which records that capture_sensor_data.py:288-293 already writes the block into simulation.json.

title: Approach-side governance by a signal or a sign
statement: Governance is readable only once a vehicle is already in the lane the device acts on: the predicate that tests it reads the `controls` edge directly, and a traffic light's `controls` edges are built from the lanes the signal affects rather than from the approach. The association is in the data but indirect - the lane a driver waits in leads into the affected lane, and the generator records that as `travelsTo`. I wanted a predicate that walks that connectivity, so a rule could say 'a red signal governs the lane the ego is approaching in' and convict a vehicle that crosses on red rather than only one already inside the affected lane. How many hops it should walk is a modelling choice, not a generator fact, so the predicate must take the depth as a parameter the way the junction-approach predicate does.
evidence: carla/schema.json governance_edges.recovering_the_approach_association, which names this a vocabulary gap and records that Pred.governs reads the `controls` edge directly.

title: Common-junction membership for two actors
statement: No predicate places two actors at the SAME junction. `Pred.inJunction` takes a junction entity, so using it for a pair means binding a junction and paying a third binder whose pairs are almost all unrelated; `Pred.inAnyJunction` quantifies the junction internally but says only that the actor is in some junction, so two vehicles at two different junctions satisfy it together. I wanted `Pred.inSameJunction (a b : EntityId) : SFProp`, true when a and b are `isIn` lanes whose roads are `isIn` one common junction node. It is buildable today from exactly the entity -> lane -> road -> junction `isIn` chain that `Pred.inJunction` already walks, over keys the adapter already lifts, and needs no adapter, capture or generator change. It would let every intersection right-of-way rule say 'these two vehicles are at the same intersection' instead of approximating it with a proximity band, which is the largest residue on both junction clauses and the one that makes them over-report.
evidence: Core/Vocab.lean section 3, where `inJunction` takes a junction entity and `inAnyJunction` quantifies it internally, and carla/schema.json reading_guide.junction_membership_and_controls, which records the road-to-junction `isIn` edge this predicate would walk. Raised by the iteration 1 coding session for Junction/yielding_to_vehicle_in_junction.
resolution: Not a capability gap — a cost preference, and cost is not a reason to leave a clause unformalized. The obligation IS expressible today by binding the entity and putting the existence condition in the antecedent: bindings are universally quantified (`RuleEntry.check` holds iff EVERY grounding holds), so `∀x. (Q x ⋀ A ⟹ B)` fires on exactly the x that satisfy Q and is vacuously true when none does — which is the reading a positive existential antecedent wants. The predicate asked for here would make that cheaper to evaluate, not newly possible, and the gate no longer rejects a schema for its grounding count. Re-file only if an obligation cannot be written at ANY binder count. NOTE the exception this reasoning does not cover: a NEGATED existential ('no device governs me', 'no lane opposes mine') is genuinely inexpressible this way, because ∀x.(¬Q x ⋀ A ⟹ B) fires per non-qualifying x rather than once when none qualifies.

title: Absence of traffic-control governance as a predicate
statement: There is no way to say 'no traffic-control device governs this vehicle', which is the antecedent of every uncontrolled-intersection clause. The only internally quantified signal predicate is `Pred.facingSignal`, which takes a state, so 'uncontrolled' has to be written as the negation of a disjunction over all five `light_state` enum values conjoined with the negation of `Pred.facingStopSign`. That is correct today but it hard-codes the enum into every rule that needs it, and it silently reads as 'no signal' for any state value outside the five. I wanted `Pred.anySignalGoverns (e : EntityId) : SFProp`, true when ANY trafficLight `controls` a lane e occupies whatever its state, and the matching form for signs, so a rule can negate one atom. Buildable today from the `controls` edge the adapter already lifts; no adapter or capture change.
evidence: Core/Vocab.lean section 8, where `facingSignal` takes a state argument and no state-free governance predicate exists, and carla/schema.json governance_edges.built_from. Raised by the iteration 1 coding session for Junction/yielding_to_vehicle_in_junction.

title: Vans carry no proximity or angular edge, so ambulances are unreachable
statement: An ambulance is a `van`, and `van` appears in neither DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS nor DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_RELATIONS, so no van is ever one end of a proximity or angular edge. Every rule whose antecedent needs a distance to an emergency vehicle can therefore only ever ground against a police car (`car`) or a firetruck (`truck`), and is blind to an ambulance no matter how close it comes. I wanted the proximity pair table to cover `van`, so that a rule saying 'an emergency vehicle is close' means all three emergency vehicle types rather than two of them. The tables are overridable parameters of `process_to_junction_rsv`, and the schema records that they are init-only and fixed before frame 0, so this cannot be recovered from captures already on disk: it needs a re-record with a wider table, which is why the owner is `capture` and not `vocab` or `adapter`. Until then both emergency clauses miss violations involving an ambulance, and the direction of that residue is under-reporting.
evidence: carla/schema.json relation_coverage.proximity_and_angular_pairs, whose excluded base classes list names `van` with the reason 'not listed in DEFAULT_PROXIMITY_RELATIONS at all', and capture_preconditions.proximity_pair_table, which records that the table is a caller-supplied init-only parameter.

title: Audible signals have no channel in the capture
statement: A siren cannot be observed in any form. There is no audio channel in the CARLA sensor set that the generator or the scene graph records, and an emergency vehicle is distinguishable only by its beacon lamps. A clause that conditions on lights AND sirens is therefore formalized on the lamps alone, which convicts a driver who did not hear and was not required to yield to a lit beacon with no siren: the residue errs toward reporting violations the law permits. This gap does not block the emergency clauses, which are formalizable with that residue stated, and both are planned this iteration. It is filed at owner `absent` so that the over-reporting direction is citable against the rule rather than inherited silently, and so that a reviewer disputing an emergency verdict has something to point at. Nothing at any layer of this pipeline can retire it; only a different simulator or a real recording with audio could.
evidence: perception/portability.json absent_from_simulator.audible_signals, which records that there is no audio channel in the CARLA sensor set the generator records and that an emergency vehicle is distinguishable only by its beacon lamps.

title: One entity's heading cannot be compared against its own earlier heading
statement: An atom sees a single Scene, so no predicate can say 'this entity is now headed opposite to the way it was headed n frames ago'. The temporal operators compare whole formulas over one fixed binding, not an entity's attribute against its own earlier value, and there is no operator that freezes a value at a position and carries it forward. The forward vector IS lifted and IS absolute on every actor-like node, so the datum is present in every frame and the obstacle is the specification language rather than the data. I wanted either a predicate over an entity and its own past, or a Core operator that binds a scene value at one position for comparison at another. Without it a direction reversal is only expressible relative to a SECOND vehicle that is present throughout and bound to one id, which is both incomplete (a reversal with no such vehicle present is invisible) and symmetric (it cannot say which of the two turned, so it convicts the ego when the other vehicle was the one that reversed). EX-TURN-001 is planned this iteration with exactly those two residues stated; retiring this would remove the symmetric one outright. Core is frozen, so this is a request for an explicit unfreeze rather than a scheduled change, and it is filed at `core` rather than `vocab` because no addition to Vocab.lean over an AtomicPred can express it.
evidence: Core/Formula.lean, whose operators are the whole temporal language and none of which binds a scene value across positions, and Core/Vocab.lean section 4b, where `headingAlignedWith` and `headingOpposedTo` both take two entities and there is no single-entity temporal form. The forward vector's presence is carla/schema.json attribute_keys fwd_x/fwd_y/fwd_z, 'unit vector component on every actor-like entity'.

title: Posted speed limit compared against a bound the rule states, without binding the sign
statement: No predicate compares a posted speed limit against a km/h bound a rule supplies, unless the sign or landmark is given a binder of its own. The internally-quantified limit predicates either only assert that some readable limit applies (Pred.hasSpeedLimitOfType, Pred.landmarkOfTypeApplies) or compare the limit against the EGO'S OWN SPEED (Pred.withinSpeedLimitOfType, Pred.exceedsSpeedLimitOfType); the predicates that do take a caller-supplied bound (Pred.landmarkStatesAtLeast / landmarkStatesAtMost, Pred.postedLimitSignAtMostKph) all require the sign as an EntityId. Pred.postedLimitSignAtMostKph applied to the VEHICLE, which is what a clause of this shape reads like, is identically FALSE: it is attrMilliLe e "posted_limit_kph" bound, and posted_limit_kph is written only on speedLimitSign nodes, so its negation is identically TRUE on every frame. I wanted Pred.speedLimitOfTypeAtLeastKph (e : EntityId) (code : String) (kph : Nat) and its AtMost companion - 'a landmark of catalogue type `code` applies to a lane `e` occupies and the limit it states is at least / at most `kph` km/h' - quantified over the frame's landmarks exactly as hasSpeedLimitOfType is, so it costs no binder. Core already computes the value: the private limitMpsOfType returns the limit in milli-m/s, unit-checked, and withinSpeedLimitOfType compares it to the ego's speed; the requested predicate differs only in comparing it to the caller's bound, using the same kph conversion Pred.speedGeKph already performs. FALSE when no readable landmark of that code applies, so it must still be paired with the existence test. Without it, a clause whose ANTECEDENT is a posted threshold cannot be written at two actor binders: the bound-sign form needs a third binder, about 8 x 10 x 6 = 480 groundings against a ~100 target. This is not specific to one clause - it is needed by every obligation triggered by a posted figure rather than by the driver's own conduct.
evidence: Core/Vocab.lean sec 9: postedLimitSignAtMostKph (~1018-1019) reads posted_limit_kph on the entity it is given; the private limitMpsOfType (~1036-1046) and withinSpeedLimitOfType; attrMilliLe on an absent attribute is false (Core/Vocab.lean ~68-72). carla/schema.json attribute_keys.posted_limit_kph is on speedLimitSign. Diagnosed by the iteration 2 coding session for Vulnerable/wider_clearance_above_fifty, which returned NO_VERDICT rather than write the unsound construction.
resolution: Not a capability gap — a cost preference, and cost is not a reason to leave a clause unformalized. The obligation IS expressible today by binding the entity and putting the existence condition in the antecedent: bindings are universally quantified (`RuleEntry.check` holds iff EVERY grounding holds), so `∀x. (Q x ⋀ A ⟹ B)` fires on exactly the x that satisfy Q and is vacuously true when none does — which is the reading a positive existential antecedent wants. The predicate asked for here would make that cheaper to evaluate, not newly possible, and the gate no longer rejects a schema for its grounding count. Re-file only if an obligation cannot be written at ANY binder count. NOTE the exception this reasoning does not cover: a NEGATED existential ('no device governs me', 'no lane opposes mine') is genuinely inexpressible this way, because ∀x.(¬Q x ⋀ A ⟹ B) fires per non-qualifying x rather than once when none qualifies.

title: Junction approach with the junction existentially quantified
statement: There is no way to say 'this vehicle is approaching some junction' without binding the junction. Pred.approachingJunctionWithin takes (hops) (e j), so a rule relating two actors at an intersection must either pay a junctionBinder as a third binder - about 8 x 8 x 4 = 256 groundings, almost every triple unrelated and therefore vacuous - or approximate 'converging on the intersection' as 'the actor is not inside any junction' plus a shared proximity band, which is what both junction nodes did. I wanted Pred.approachingAnyJunctionWithin (hops : Nat) (e : EntityId), the existentially quantified form, and the paired Pred.approachingSameJunctionWithin (hops : Nat) (a b : EntityId) for the two-actor case. Buildable today from exactly the travelsTo connectivity Pred.approachingJunctionWithin already walks, over keys the adapter already lifts; no adapter, capture or generator change. Distinct from G8, which is about two actors being members of one common junction, not about either of them approaching one - a rule about arrival at an intersection needs both, since a vehicle that has not yet entered the junction is a member of no junction at all. This gap does NOT block its clauses: both are formalizable today with the proximity approximation and its over-reporting direction stated on the node, so their rows stay pending. It is filed so the residue is citable and so the next iteration does not re-derive the same predicate from scratch.
evidence: Core/Vocab.lean sec 3: approachingJunctionWithin (hops e j), inAnyJunction, inJunction. Core/Grounding.lean junctionBinder, about 4 candidates, against check_spec.CAPTURE_ENTITY_CENSUS and GROUNDING_BUDGET. carla/schema.json junction_membership_and_controls: the graph settles no reach of its own, the hop count is caller-supplied. Named from the rule's side by the iteration 2 coding session for Junction/simultaneous_arrival_yield_right.

The obligation IS expressible today by binding the entity and putting the existence condition in the antecedent: bindings are universally quantified (`RuleEntry.check` holds iff EVERY grounding holds), so `∀x. (Q x ⋀ A ⟹ B)` fires on exactly the x that satisfy Q and is vacuously true when none does — which is the reading a positive existential antecedent wants. The predicate asked for here would make that cheaper to evaluate, not newly possible, and the gate no longer rejects a schema for its grounding count. Re-file only if an obligation cannot be written at ANY binder count. NOTE the exception this reasoning does not cover: a NEGATED existential ('no device governs me', 'no lane opposes mine') is genuinely inexpressible this way, because ∀x.(¬Q x ⋀ A ⟹ B) fires per non-qualifying x rather than once when none qualifies.

title: Off-roadway surface type discarded by the abstraction
statement: Nothing in the trace distinguishes one non-driving surface from another. process_to_junction_rsv filters out Sidewalk nodes, keeps only Driving ones, and attaches every actor with no driving-lane edge to the SINGLE `Off Road` node, so pavement, verge, central reservation, shoulder, lay-by, parking bay and private ground are one indistinguishable region in Lean. I wanted the waypoint's lane_type - which the BASE graph already carries as `sem_class` on its waypoint nodes - to survive the fold, as an attribute on the off-roadway node an actor is `isIn`, or as distinct off-roadway node kinds. That would let a rule say 'the ego is standing on a footway' as opposed to 'the ego is standing somewhere that is not a driving lane', which is the difference between the surfaces a parking prohibition names and the ones it permits. The datum is computed and then thrown away, not missing, so this is not `unsupported`. It is filed at owner `capture` on the same grounds as G4: the value lives on the base graph, the adapter reads the RSV and cannot reach it, and carla_sgg is frozen byte-wise, so the route is a collector of our own reading the base graph before it is folded - which cannot be recovered from captures already on disk. This gap does NOT block EX-PARK-001: that clause is formalizable today with the over-reporting residue stated, and it is planned this iteration as Parking/off_roadway_dwell. It is filed so that the residue - a lawful parking bay convicted as a sidewalk, the largest single residue in the corpus - is citable against the rule rather than inherited silently.
evidence: carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py:133-134 keeps only Driving nodes and filters Sidewalk out; :248 attaches any actor with no driving-lane edge to the single `Off Road` node. carla/schema.json -> off_road_node data limit states the collapse. perception/portability.json -> off_roadway_surface_type, origin in_base_not_rsv.

title: Actor body geometry, so a clearance is measured between node centres
statement: Every metric separation this library can compute is centre-to-centre. carla/adapter.py lifts `vertex` as pos_x/pos_y/pos_z and Pred.withinCentimetres / beyondCentimetres / withinMetresExact square the difference of those points, so a clause stating a clearance between two road users is evaluated between the centres of two bodies rather than between their nearest surfaces. The error is roughly the sum of the two half-extents along the line of separation - on the order of two metres for a car beside a cyclist - which is LARGER than the clearance figures traffic codes state, so it is not a rounding matter. I wanted `threedbbox` lifted (or, better, a pair of half-extent keys derived from it by the adapter) together with a Pred.clearanceAtLeastCentimetres over the two bodies, so a rule can state the clearance the clause states. `threedbbox` is on the unlifted side of carla/schema.json's key partition, i.e. present in the data and not in Lean, which makes this a vocabulary-and-adapter extension and NOT an unsupported clause. The schema's own note calls it redundant because `vertex` already gives the box centre; that is true for a position and false for a clearance, which is the distinction this gap turns on. Retiring it needs an adapter entry, a portability class beside it and one predicate in Vocab.lean; no capture or generator change. This gap does NOT block a clearance clause outright - EX-VULNERABLE-001 is formalized today from the centre separation - but it is the residue on every such rule, and the direction is UNDER-REPORTING: a pass whose surfaces were 0.4 m apart is measured as comfortably over a metre and reads compliant. It is not specific to one clause; every obligation stating a lateral or longitudinal clearance inherits it.
evidence: carla/schema.json -> available_not_exposed.volume.threedbbox ('8 corners x 3 components = 24 numbers per node per frame, from parse3dbb / get_local_vertices'), against node_coordinates, which records that only `vertex` is lifted as pos_x/pos_y/pos_z. Core/Vocab.lean sepSqMilli / withinCentimetres / beyondCentimetres compute from posMilli alone.

title: Lane ordinal within a carriageway, without binding a lane
statement: There is no way to say how many same-direction lanes lie to each side of the one a vehicle occupies. Pred.inOutermostLane and Pred.hasLaneToTheSide look one lane across, because the abstraction emits `toLeftOf` / `toRightOf` only between ADJACENT lane ids of one road, so the strongest statement available is 'there is no same-direction lane immediately to my left'. A clause that distinguishes the right-hand lanes from the centre lane, or the centre lane from the leftmost, cannot be written from that: on a carriageway of three, the centre lane satisfies 'not the leftmost' exactly as the rightmost does. I wanted Pred.sameDirectionLanesToTheSide (side : RelLabel) (e : EntityId) (n : Nat), true when at least n same-direction lanes lie on that side of the lane e occupies, walking the adjacency chain transitively and quantifying every lane internally so the rule pays no lane binder - binding lanes for this costs laneBinder x laneBinder at about 1,190 groundings against a ~100 target, and almost every pair is unrelated. It is buildable today from exactly the adjacency edges Pred.laneBesideSameDirection already reads, over keys the adapter already lifts; no adapter, capture or generator change. The lane_id sign is not a substitute and the schema marks it DO NOT USE for direction. This is distinct from G5, which is about whether a road is a freeway at all; this gap is about position within the carriageway once the lane structure is known, and a lane-choice clause needs both. It does not block a 'not the leftmost lane' reading, which is formalized today, but that reading UNDER-REPORTS: a driver in the centre lane of three is not convicted where the clause requires a right-hand lane.
evidence: carla/schema.json -> inter_lane_left_right_edges: 'Lane-to-lane toLeftOf / toRightOf ... carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py:161 pairs consecutive sorted lane ids', and its DO NOT USE note on the lane_id sign. Core/Vocab.lean 3a: laneBesideSameDirection / inOutermostLane / hasLaneToTheSide are the only lateral predicates and all look exactly one lane across.

The obligation IS expressible today by binding the entity and putting the existence condition in the antecedent: bindings are universally quantified (`RuleEntry.check` holds iff EVERY grounding holds), so `∀x. (Q x ⋀ A ⟹ B)` fires on exactly the x that satisfy Q and is vacuously true when none does — which is the reading a positive existential antecedent wants. The predicate asked for here would make that cheaper to evaluate, not newly possible, and the gate no longer rejects a schema for its grounding count. Re-file only if an obligation cannot be written at ANY binder count. NOTE the exception this reasoning does not cover: a NEGATED existential ('no device governs me', 'no lane opposes mine') is genuinely inexpressible this way, because ∀x.(¬Q x ⋀ A ⟹ B) fires per non-qualifying x rather than once when none qualifies.

title: Carriageway side: a one-way or non-opposed roadway, without binding a lane
statement: There is no way to say that the roadway a vehicle occupies carries no traffic in the opposite direction. `Pred.opposingLanes (a b : EntityId)` takes two ACTORS and is listed beside `Pred.sameLane` in Core/Vocab.lean section 3, so it reports that two bound road users are in opposing lanes -- a statement about who happens to be present, not about the road. A clause whose exception is conditioned on the roadway itself therefore has no antecedent to read: with no opposing vehicle in the trace the predicate is false, and it is false in exactly the same way on a one-way street and on an empty two-way road. I wanted Pred.roadHasNoOpposingLane (e : EntityId) : SFProp, true when no lane reachable along the same-road adjacency chain from the lane e occupies `opposes` it, with every lane quantified internally so the rule pays no lane binder -- binding lanes for this costs laneBinder x laneBinder at about 1,190 groundings against a ~100 target. It must walk the chain TRANSITIVELY and not one hop: carla/schema.json's inter_lane_left_right_edges section records that `opposes`, `toLeftOf` and `toRightOf` are emitted only between ADJACENT lane ids of one road, so on a carriageway of two the outer lane is adjacent to no opposing lane and a one-hop test would call it one-way. That is the same transitivity G17 asks for over the same edges, and the two are distinct: G17 counts same-direction lanes to one side, this one asks whether any opposing lane exists at all. Buildable today from the `opposes` edges the adapter already lifts and the `.opposes` RelLabel in Core/Scene.lean; no adapter, capture or generator change. The OTHER half of the same exception -- a DIVIDED highway -- is not reachable at this owner and is deliberately NOT re-proposed here: it rests on a median, which the abstraction records in no node, edge or attribute, and the route to it is the waypoint lane_type surviving the fold, which G15 already asks for. So retiring this gap removes the one-way half of the exception and leaves the divided-highway half on G15.
evidence: Core/Vocab.lean section 3 (opposingLanes takes two actors, exactly as sameLane does; no internally-quantified form exists); Core/Scene.lean RelLabel `.opposes`; carla/schema.json -> inter_lane_left_right_edges, both its `mechanism` (sgg_abstractor.py:161 pairs consecutive sorted lane ids) and its DO NOT USE note forbidding the lane_id sign for direction; state/ReformV2/iter_004/objectives.jsonl, residue (a) on Emergency/pull_to_rightmost_lane.

title: Time gap between two actors, scaled by the follower's own speed
statement: No predicate expresses a separation requirement that scales with the subject's own speed, so a durational headway obligation cannot be stated as the duration it is. The vocabulary compares a separation against a CONSTANT bound (Pred.beyondCentimetres, withinMetresExact, withinMetres) and compares a speed against a constant bound (Pred.speedGeKph, speedLe), and there is no multiplication anywhere between them, so 'at least N seconds of space' has to be written as a step function: a disjunction over ego speed bands, each band conjoined with the constant separation N seconds at that band requires. That is expressible today and is how Following/two_second_gap is planned this iteration, but the banding is a quantization the clause does not contain, every boundary has to be resolved toward permitting so the rule does not convict a compliant driver, and the band table has to be re-derived by hand for every different N. I wanted Pred.timeGapAtLeastSeconds (a b : EntityId) (seconds : Nat), true when the separation between a and b is at least the distance a travels in `seconds` at its current speed. It is buildable today over keys the adapter already lifts and arithmetic Core already performs: Pred.sepSqMilli gives the exact squared separation in milli-units from pos_x/pos_y/pos_z, `speed` is lifted on the ego in milli-m/s, and comparing sepSq against (speed * seconds)^2 keeps the whole test in the integer milli-unit arithmetic Core/Decimal.lean already uses, with no square root and no Float. No adapter, capture or generator change. This is not specific to one clause: every obligation stating a following distance, a headway or a stopping distance as a time rather than a distance inherits the same banding, and a jurisdiction that states two-second and three-second gaps needs two hand-built band tables where one predicate would serve both.
evidence: Core/Vocab.lean sections 4 and 6 as rendered in the plan prompt: every separation predicate (withinMetres, withinCentimetres, beyondCentimetres, withinMetresExact) takes a constant bound and every speed predicate (speedLe, speedGe, speedLeKph, speedGeKph) compares against a constant, with no predicate taking both; Pred.sepSqMilli and Pred.posMilli already expose the exact squared separation, and `speed` is on the lifted side of carla/schema.json's attribute_keys partition (decimal, m/s, ego only).

title: Lane direction of travel, so a heading can be compared against the roadway
statement: No lane node says which way traffic runs along it in any geometric sense, so a vehicle's absolute heading cannot be compared against the road it is on. carla/schema.json's reading_guide.angular_edges_and_lane_connectivity states the consequence outright -- 'No lane node carries a direction vector, so an actor's absolute heading cannot be compared with its own lane' -- and reading_guide.node_coordinates gives the mechanism: structure nodes carry NO attributes at all, because sgg_abstractor.py builds them as Node(name=...) with the attr default and the class defines attr = {} when none is passed. The `travelsTo` edge between lane nodes does state a direction of travel, but it is topological and the lane nodes it joins have no coordinates, so no bearing can be recovered from it. I wanted the lane's direction of travel as a vector on the lane node a vehicle is `isIn` -- or, equivalently, the pair of predicates Pred.headingAlignedWithLane (e : EntityId) and Pred.headingOpposedToLane (e : EntityId), with the lane quantified internally so the rule pays no lane binder. The datum is computable on the BASE graph, which samples each lane at `segment_length` and computes a turn angle per waypoint from the vectors to its neighbours (carla_sgg/sgg.py:314-339); process_to_junction_rsv folds every waypoint of a lane into one attribute-free node and keeps none of it. That is why the owner is `capture` and not `vocab` or `adapter`, on exactly the grounds carla/schema.json gives for the in_base_not_rsv class and the same grounds G4 and G15 are filed on: the adapter reads the RSV and cannot reach the base graph, carla_sgg is frozen byte-wise, so the route is a collector of our own reading the base graph before the fold -- which cannot be recovered from captures already on disk. This gap does NOT block EX-TURN-001: that clause is planned this iteration as Turn/uturn_interference, which reads the reversal relative to a second vehicle bound for the whole trace. It is filed because retiring it would remove BOTH of that node's G12 residues at once -- the under-reporting one (a U-turn with no second vehicle present is invisible) and the over-reporting one (aligned-then-opposed is symmetric, so the rule convicts the ego when the OTHER vehicle reversed) -- and it would do so without the Core unfreeze G12 asks for, since comparing a heading against the lane it occupies is a single-Scene test an AtomicPred can see. Distinct from G4, which asks for the CURVATURE of the road rather than its direction, and from G12, which asks to compare an entity against its own past; a reversal is readable from either, and this is the cheaper of the two layers.
evidence: carla/schema.json reading_guide.angular_edges_and_lane_connectivity (data_limit: no lane node carries a direction vector) and reading_guide.node_coordinates (data_limit: structure nodes carry no attributes at all, sgg_abstractor.py:19-23 and the attribute-free Node(name=...) constructions at :145, :147, :152); carla_sgg/sgg.py:314-339 for the per-waypoint geometry on the base graph; perception/portability.json road_curvature and off_roadway_surface_type for the in_base_not_rsv origin and what retiring it takes; Core/Vocab.lean section 4b, which has headingAlignedWith and headingOpposedTo over two ACTORS and no counterpart over an actor and its lane.

title: Relative bearing to another actor against a caller-supplied sector
statement: Left and right of the ego are readable only through the generator's fixed 90-degree sector split, and a clause that turns on which of two converging vehicles is on the right is decided within noise of a sector edge. The angular edges are computed from the source actor's forward vector and bucketed by DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_THRESHOLDS (carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py:185-195), which carla/schema.json capture_preconditions.directional_split_degrees records as an overridable parameter that no capture records; Pred.toLeftOf and Pred.toRightOf read the resulting edge label and nothing else. A vehicle approaching a crossroads perpendicularly sits exactly ON the boundary between the side sector and the front sector, so the single fact an uncontrolled-intersection priority clause turns on is the least robust thing the abstraction reports, and perception/portability.json heading records that a sector boundary is not robust to a 10-degree orientation error. I wanted Pred.bearingWithinSector (a b : EntityId) (side : RelLabel) (halfWidthDegrees : Nat) -- true when the displacement from a to b falls within a caller-supplied half-width of a's lateral axis on the named side -- so a rule can require the other actor to be WELL inside the side sector rather than anywhere in a sector whose edge the capture chose. It is buildable today over keys the adapter already lifts: Pred.posMilli and Pred.vecMilli already return the position and the forward vector in integer milli-units, Pred.sepSqMilli already squares a displacement, and a sector test is the sign of a cross product against a scaled dot product, which needs no trigonometry, no square root and no Float -- exactly the integer milli-unit arithmetic Core/Decimal.lean already performs. No adapter, capture or generator change. It also removes the dependence on the capture's directional threshold table, which is init-only, fixed before frame 0 and recorded nowhere in a capture, so today every left-or-right verdict in this library silently inherits a setting nothing can confirm. This gap does NOT block its clause: EX-JUNCTION-002 is planned this iteration as Junction/simultaneous_arrival with the sector residue stated, and that residue errs BOTH ways -- it can convict the vehicle that was on the right and miss the one that was on the left. It is filed so the residue is citable against the rule rather than inherited silently, and because it is not specific to one clause: every obligation that distinguishes the two sides of a vehicle -- priority at an uncontrolled junction, passing on a particular side, a lateral clearance to one side -- reads the same three labels.
evidence: carla/schema.json reading_guide.angular_edges_and_lane_connectivity (mechanism: sgg_abstractor.py:185-195, arcs from DEFAULT_DIRECTIONAL_THRESHOLDS; data_limit: a mutual angular pair is symmetric) and capture_preconditions.directional_split_degrees (overridable, recorded in no capture, and 'Pred.oncoming's 90 degrees is a property of that table'); Core/Vocab.lean section 5, where toLeftOf and toRightOf are the raw edge and nothing parameterises the sector, and sections 4 and 4b, where posMilli, vecMilli and sepSqMilli already expose the vectors in integer milli-units; perception/portability.json heading ('a sector boundary at 45 degrees is not robust to a 10-degree orientation error').

title: Junction boundary nodes are not parsed, so arrival at an intersection has no position
statement: Nothing in the trace marks where a junction begins, so 'has arrived at the intersection' and 'arrived at the same time' have no representation and both junction rules approximate them with junction OCCUPANCY plus a shared proximity band. I wanted a positioned node at each junction entry, which the generator can already build: init_to_world(parse_junction_boundaries=True) walks outward from every junction waypoint and creates a `junction_boundary_<junction_id>_<node>` node through __add_to_graph at the mean of the outside and inside waypoints (carla_sgg/sgg.py:360-405), joined by `isIn` edges to the driving nodes on both sides. Because it goes through __add_to_graph it carries `vertex` and `forward` like any actor, which is what every structure node lacks, so a metric distance from a vehicle to the junction mouth becomes computable. The rest of the chain already exists: get_base_type returns the blueprint for a 'junction_boundary' (carla_sgg/actors.py:37), process_to_junction_rsv keeps it as an actor rather than filtering it (sgg_abstractor.py:131-132 drops only Driving and Sidewalk), carla/adapter.py:370-376 maps it to `.junctionBoundary`, and Core/Scene.lean:68 already has the constructor. The single reason no capture has one is that the flag defaults to False. That makes this `capture` and not `adapter` or `generator`: the parameter is init-only and fixed before frame 0 (carla/schema.json capture_preconditions.when_they_are_fixed), so it cannot be recovered from captures already on disk and needs a re-record with the flag set -- plus a binder or an internally quantified predicate, since Core/Grounding.lean::unboundEntityTypes excludes `.junctionBoundary` for exactly the reason this gap names. Retiring it would let a rule say 'this vehicle crossed into the junction' and 'that vehicle crossed before this one', replacing the occupancy-plus-proximity approximation that OVER-REPORTS on both junction nodes. Distinct from G2, which asks for the halt position a stop sign or signal requires -- a stop line sits back from the junction and comes from get_stop_waypoints, a different call the generator never makes; and distinct from G8 and G14, which ask for membership and approach predicates over structure nodes that carry no position at all and so can never express an arrival ORDER however they are quantified.
evidence: carla_sgg/sgg.py:146 init_to_world(parse_junction_boundaries=False) and :360-405 the boundary-node construction; carla_sgg/actors.py:37; carla_sgg/sgg_abstractor.py:131-132; carla/adapter.py:370-376; library/TrafficSpec/Core/Scene.lean:68 and Core/Grounding.lean::unboundEntityTypes; carla/schema.json capture_preconditions.junction_boundaries and .when_they_are_fixed; residues (r1)/(r2) in library/TrafficSpec/Rules/Junction/arrived_first.lean and (r1)/(r2) in Junction/simultaneous_arrival.lean

title: Ego's own light state, so its indicated direction of travel is unreadable
statement: The ego vehicle carries no light_* attribute of any kind, so nothing in the trace says what the ego indicated it was about to do. carla_sgg/sgg.py writes one boolean per member of carla.VehicleLightState.names for every carla.Vehicle reached by the actor loop, and generate_graph_for_frame appends self.ego_id to exclude_ids unconditionally (sgg.py:543-544) while the loop filters on actor.id not in exclude_ids (:575), so the ego is never in it - carla/schema.json states the consequence directly in attribute_keys ('boolean on every vehicle EXCEPT the ego') and in capture_preconditions.excluded_actors ('The ego is always appended to it, which is WHY the ego carries no light_* attributes'). Every OTHER vehicle's blinkers and brake lamp ARE lifted and are the only dynamic evidence about it, so the abstraction is inverted exactly where it matters: the one vehicle whose conduct every rule in this library judges is the one whose signalled intention is invisible. I wanted the ego's light booleans on the ego node, which would give Pred.leftBlinkerOn / rightBlinkerOn / brakeLightOn / hazardLightsOn a meaning on the subject of every rule, and would let a clause about a signalled manoeuvre - turning, changing lane, pulling over, proceeding straight - read the driver's declared intention rather than inferring it from the wheel angle. Today the only substitute is `steer`, which reports the wheel angle and not the path: a wide-radius turn through a large junction holds a small steering angle and reads as straight ahead, and a lane change and a curve are indistinguishable from each other. carla.Vehicle.get_light_state() exists on every vehicle actor including the one chosen as ego, so the datum is in the simulator and not in the graph. carla_sgg is frozen byte-wise, so the route is a collector of our own calling get_light_state on the ego at capture time; it cannot be recovered from captures already on disk, which is why the owner is `capture` and not `adapter` or `vocab`. This gap does NOT block its clause: EX-SIGNAL-002 is formalizable today and is planned this iteration as Signal/green_before_straight, reading 'proceeding straight ahead' from `steer` with the over-reporting residue stated on the node. It is filed so that residue is citable rather than inherited, and because it is not specific to one clause - every obligation about a signalled manoeuvre by the subject vehicle inherits it. Distinct from every open gap in the ledger: G3 asks for a non-ego motion state, which is the mirror of this and about other vehicles; nothing filed asks for the ego's own light channel.
evidence: carla/schema.json -> attribute_keys (light_* keys, 'on every vehicle EXCEPT the ego'), reading_guide.vehicle_light_booleans (mechanism: sgg.py:689, :543-544, :575, :562-563), capture_preconditions.excluded_actors; Core/Vocab.lean s7; perception/portability.json (the light_* keys are the portable class, so this is also the cheapest evidence to carry to real video)
